messages:
Carlos (CTO): Thanks for the great turnout on the all-hands. Posting a focused thread for the runtime/kernel SLAs and rollout Qs we didn't get to. Keep answers short.
Leah (VP Eng): Two bullets folks asked: measurement (p95 vs p99) and whether batching changes are global or per-model.
Sam (Eng Lead): Quick: we will publish both p95 and p99 for transparency. SLA enforcement will be on p99 for Dedicated, p95 for hosted tiers for now.
Jing (Runtime): Clarify measurement window: are we using a rolling 5m, 1m, or 60s?
Marta (SRE): We'll use a 60s rolling window for alerting and a 5m window for SLA reporting to smooth spikes. Alerts trigger on sustained breaches across both.
Theo (Kernel): Rollout question: do we prefer model-size first (small->large) or architecture family first?
Sam (Eng Lead): Prioritize by impact: kernel wins (latency/cost) > regression risk. So we do biggest-percentage-improvement first regardless of size, but separate canaries per family to limit cross-model risk.
Jing (Runtime): Batching defaults: what's the target batch size and dynamic threshold for switching to batching vs low-latency path?
Sam (Eng Lead): Default dynamic batching: target batch_size=32 for gen workloads, but we use latency SLO to choose fast-path if queueing latency > 10ms. Customers on Dedicated can tune via pool config.
Marta (SRE): Note: batching decisions are also hardware-dependent; A100 vs L4 have different sweet spots. We surface hardware profiles in the console.
Leah (VP Eng): Customers worried about regressions during kernel rollouts on Dedicated. What's the rollback behavior?
Theo (Kernel): For Dedicated pools we do staged rollout: 1% traffic (30m), 10% (1h), 50% (2h), 100% (if green). Auto-rollback triggers if p95 increases >12% or error rate rises 0.5% absolute during a stage. Pools are pinned by default; upgrades require explicit opt-in unless customer agreed to auto-updates.
Jing (Runtime): KV cache migration question: if kernel changes alter serialization, how long is the compatibility window?
Theo (Kernel): We plan a 72h mixed-compatibility window and run a validation cohort. We'll mark breaking changes as major and schedule maintenance windows.
Carlos (CTO): Observability ask: what dashboards will be public/internal and where do teams look for per-customer regressions?
Marta (SRE): Internal: latency.p95/p99, batch_size_distribution, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kernel_version_per_node, per-pool error_rate. We'll add a per-customer incident view in the console for Dedicated.
Ops Bot: deploy/canary-started kernel-opt-v3 us-east-1 1% -> monitoring: https://internal.monitor/1890012345
Sam (Eng Lead): Action: I'll file the SLO doc and batching guide to #docs-runtime and link it here.
Leah (VP Eng): I'll update customer comms template for Dedicated pinning and safe-upgrade opt-in.
Theo (Kernel): I'll publish the kernel rollout playbook and the migration checklist by EOD.
Carlos (CTO): If there are any remaining quick Qs post-live Q&A, drop them here and we'll follow up in the thread. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
